borrow.hook_logic: Beat 0 sets a compressed challenge and promises the speaker's own method: if you had to learn this in one day, here is how I do it. We keep the promise of a method that runs today and drop the hypothetical, and we open on the screen instead of the face, because the 35 reels whose first visual state is a screen carry median share rate 0.0213 against 0.0140 (insight I-09).
borrow.proof_mechanism: Beats 2 to 4 run definition, then a person shaped analogy, then a one line callback, and beat 3 carries the whole reel on a contrasting pair of questions: Bob can tell you how big Central Park is, and cannot tell you where your company's IT desk is until you hand him your documents. That pair is what we borrow whole. The second thing we borrow is that the reel finishes one complete unit of teaching on screen rather than promising it after the keyword, which is why it holds the highest save rate in the batch at 58 saves per thousand plays.
borrow.ordering: Screen first, then the pair of questions, then the fix run live on the second ask, then the one line rule, then beat 5's rehook that this applies everywhere an answer leaves the building, then the keyword last. The reference puts its own call at 56.2 of 58.4 seconds, and 94 % of the 216 CTAs in the corpus sit in the last quarter (insight I-12).
borrow.visual_grammar: From the frames: captions in the top third for the whole reel (text overlay density 1.0), the lesson page stacked above the facecam at scene 4, a plain screen recording of the tool as proof at scene 8. We take the screen above face arrangement for the two answers side by side and the top third captions, we do not open on split screen (the niche's most used and weakest opening state, median robust_z 1.03 against 1.43, insight I-10), and we come back to camera for the boundary and the keyword (face, screen, face carries median share rate 0.0213 against 0.0140, p=0.00076, insight I-11). The floating pink keyword tags at scenes 1 and 2 are the one element we refuse: they are a glossary of the exact words rule 13 keeps out of the first ten seconds.

change.process: The check that happens to Marta's work after it leaves her desk in a 15 to 60 person services company. She writes the recommendation out of the handbook, the signed contract or the HRIS export, sends it up, and the owner pastes the same question into his own chat before he replies to her. Owner of the process is Marta, because she is the one who has to answer for the difference.
change.friction: The owner's chat answered about the industry, not about this company: nobody attached the handbook or the contract, so it returned the general default, and Marta spends the afternoon defending an answer that was already right. Her file records the pattern at 113 points, boss uses AI for everything and checked her HR advice against Claude, and her team has stopped reading the summaries anyway, which means the wrong answer travels further than the right one.
change.ai_boundary: The machine reads the documents it is handed and has to name the document, the clause and the date it came from, and say which document it could not find an answer in. It does not decide which source governs when the handbook and the signed contract disagree; that is Marta's call and it is said out loud on camera. It never sees the client's own file, because the memo on her desk says no client data goes into any of these tools. Nobody's job moves anywhere. What comes back is the afternoon.
change.next_action: Comment SOURCES, and the next time it happens attach the handbook and ask the same question again, then send both answers up side by side with the clause marked.

hook: Here is the reply when your boss checks your work against a chat: the chat never saw the handbook, so give it the handbook.

on_screen.opening_screen: The boss's chat window full width, his question and a confident answer that is wrong for this company, and next to it the page of our own handbook that says otherwise, with the owner's name and the review date printed on it. No face for the first few seconds.
on_screen.human_check: The same question asked a second time with the handbook, the signed contract and the policy attached, and the two answers put side by side on screen. The rule on the overlay: an answer counts only when it names the document and the clause it came from. One answer is rejected live because the clause it quoted is not in the document. Then the line a person keeps, which source governs when two of them disagree, and whether it goes out at all.
on_screen.cost_line: Nothing on top of the licence already sitting on her desk, and $20 a month is the personal ceiling she funds herself. It stops paying at the line her IT memo draws: the moment the answer needs the client's own file, the sources cannot be attached and this is guesswork again.
